title: TrustCarbon
subtitle: Carbon emissions analysis and corporate disclosure review
points: Phase IV Mini Project
Group 39
Jainam Bhavsar, Adil Khan, Aditya Chavan
notes: Introduce the project in one sentence. Move quickly to the problem. Prepared on 29 October 2026 against the supplied Phase IV rubric.

title: Problem and objectives
points: Carbon records use different units, years and reporting formats.
TrustCarbon makes historical patterns and their sources easier to inspect.
Private accounts support personal records and dataset review.
notes: Explain why provenance and reporting periods matter. Historical observations, corporate disclosures and scenarios have different meanings.

title: Application architecture
points: React and Recharts provide the interactive dashboard.
Service modules connect forms and source requests to backend operations.
Supabase Auth identifies accounts. PostgreSQL stores records. Private Storage holds CSV files.
notes: Explain the data path: form input, service, Supabase API, database policy, response, refreshed React state. Source: src/App.jsx, src/services, src/config/supabase.js.

title: Database and access control
points: Profiles own activities, datasets and alert rules.
Administrators review pending dataset submissions.
Row-level policies enforce ownership independently of route visibility.
notes: Show the schema table in REPORT.html. Explain foreign keys, indexes and status constraints. Source: supabase/migrations/. Demonstrate two-account isolation using TESTING.md.

title: Historical exploration
points: Country comparisons preserve year, unit and source labels.
Time Machine supports playback and baseline comparisons.
Source failure activates a labelled historical CSV fallback.
notes: Switch to the live app. Select India and a reporting year. Explain gaps rather than inventing missing values. Sources: src/services/owidService.js and trustCarbonDataService.js.

title: Live integration demonstration
points: Create a disposable activity and reload the page.
Edit its emissions value and confirm the saved change after reload.
Delete the disposable record and confirm that it stays absent.
notes: Use the test commute described in DEMO_GUIDE.md. This is the key persistence demonstration for the 10-mark integration component. Complete the database migration before presenting.

title: Dataset and disclosure workflow
points: CSV validation rejects incomplete or invalid submissions.
Private uploads enter an administrator review queue.
Corporate PDF candidates require confirmation with page and reporting-period evidence.
notes: Use the clearly labelled synthetic CSV fixtures. Show the invalid case first, then a valid pending submission and admin decision. Corporate documents remain in session state. Source: datasetService.js, brsrIngestionService.js and migrations.

title: Testing evidence
points: Automated calculation and service checks accompany the submission.
Regression cases cover blank values, retries and upload cleanup.
A 150,000-row CSV case checks large-input validation.
notes: Open evidence/verification.json and test-results.json for current counts and timings. Service tests use mocked responses. Do not present those as live database integration tests.

title: Reliability and current limits
points: Network timeouts and visible errors bound failed requests.
Compact navigation supports smaller windows.
Live account persistence, Storage and isolation need recorded acceptance checks.
notes: Show /data/system and the completed testing record. Connection SELECT probes do not establish write permissions or full account isolation. Historical data is not a real-time emissions feed.

title: Results and next steps
points: One workspace connects emissions exploration with evidence review.
Phase IV materials include the report, test logs and a repeatable demo.
Future work includes durable corporate documents, OCR and scheduled monitoring.
notes: Finish with actual demonstrated outcomes. Keep the report and test evidence available for questions. Acknowledge any acceptance check that remains pending.
